findings.message: A different agent (Claude) checked the work in a separate headless process.

The CI-backed provenance design handles the earlier blocking finding well. It refuses arbitrary uploads, keeps the signing job separate and explains its freshness limits. The rest of the planning packet was not updated to match it. The ticket scope and done_when, the spec, the scenarios and the dimensions still describe the withdrawn approach: reuse the local signer, say the fabricated-execution design is unresolved, and treat the operator account as fully trusted. Read that way, the accepted contract can still be met by an implementation that the design itself calls insufficient. These documents need to be reconciled before the next planning review.

The ticket and spec do not require trusted execution provenance, so the accepted contract can be met by the rejected design. ticket.md scope says to 'reuse authenticated observation, certification, revocation and local closing checks'. Its done_when only refuses 'self-issued' evidence. provenance-result.md now says re-signing identical approved content is not self-issued forgery. review-disposition.md says the shared signer 'cannot distinguish a real run from equivalent fabricated fields'. Under this wording, an implementation that reuses the shared signer plus a fresh independent review could satisfy every done_when item, while a candidate fabricates execution and gets a fresh approval. That is exactly the case the accepted review finding requires to be refused. Fix: rewrite scope, done_when and spec R2 to require execution provenance from a trusted, separately controlled producer (or an equivalent stated boundary). Record the user's scope decision about the new CI producer/import adapter and the required online synchronization step.

The scenarios contradict each other on the trust model. scenarios-draft.md R2 still says 'Compromise of the operator's entire account/key store is outside the existing trust model; this feature does not add a separate signing service or OS security boundary.' The next scenario still says the fabricated-execution 'design remains unresolved'. Candidate code runs as the operator by default (provenance-result.md correction), so treating the operator account as trusted makes 'Fabricated execution cannot become authentic through a fresh review' unattainable. That leaves two incompatible ways to implement it. Meanwhile ci-provenance-design.md does add an isolation boundary (a container plus a separate CI signer). Fix: update the scenarios to the CI design. Remove or narrow the 'operator account trusted' carve-out, and state which actor the boundary defends against.

dimensions.md and completeness-check.md still list the accepted Verifier origin / Execution provenance partition as an 'independently reviewed installed runtime outside candidate' with 'authenticated' execution. They do not mention the attestation's workflow identity or revision, the run attempt, the import/cache state, or the refusal of arbitrary uploads. ci-provenance-design.md's proof plan has these partitions, but they have not been carried into the scenario and dimension sets that will be promoted.

Spec Surfaces says 'OpenCode/cloud eligibility stays excluded', and a scenario says unsupported producers stay excluded. The new design makes GitHub Actions, a cloud execution environment, the required producer. State explicitly that the trusted CI workflow is the one supported execution producer, separate from excluded cloud hosts. Otherwise the 'Excluded hosts and producers' scenario either contradicts the design or becomes ambiguous.

The design does not say how CI attempts are selected. It covers revocation by a later known failed attempt and admits that offline closing cannot see unsynced runs. It does not say what happens when a candidate SHA has earlier failed or interrupted attempts followed by a passing one: whether retrying until a run passes is allowed, and which attempt counts as current. 'Require explicit synchronization before final completion' is not tied to any recorded sync state or age bound that closing checks. Without that, closing could accept a stale import even though the sync requirement is claimed. Define the attempt-selection rule and bind sync state into the authenticated validation state.

The isolation evidence (isolation-feasibility.md) comes from local OrbStack/Docker probes. On a GitHub-hosted runner, the controller process holds ACTIONS_RUNTIME_TOKEN and GITHUB_TOKEN, and the execution job uploads the artifact that the signing job then trusts. The design says feasibility must be proven, but its first acceptance boundary should also cover that runner-level token exposure and artifact integrity between the two jobs, not just the absence of credentials inside the container.

ticket.md's work log has only its creation entry. It does not record the planning review 628139a4, the withdrawn decision, or the change to a CI design. completeness-check.md's original 'rejected for missing trusted execution provenance' wording is corrected only in provenance-result.md, so readers should be pointed to that correction.
